lines.trans: Viktor, you are behaving very rudely!
I treat all women wonderfully.
Then why do you insult me like that?
You will not be able to work a whole day.
Then let us bet right now!
What do you want to bet about with me?
I will work a full shift in the kitchen.
My cooks will quickly break your pride.
If I cope, you will pay for dinner!
And if you run away after an hour?
Then you will win our main bet.
Agreed, tomorrow I expect you in the kitchen!
All viewers will be witnesses of our bet.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

вести.gloss: to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)

meanings.en: to lead, to guide, to drive
meanings.note: Unidirectional verb of motion. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lead, to conduct (вести себя = to behave)', paired with 'повести'.

meanings.en: вести себя: to behave, to conduct oneself
meanings.note: Вы как маленькая себя ведёте = You're behaving like a little girl

examples.trans: You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
after a plural noun or pronoun: вы все
Всем = to everyone (dative). Core Russian pron meaning 'all; everyone' in everyday speech.

examples.text: И знаешь, что самое главное? Всем всё равно.
examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.
examples.trans: Pasha, you won't win this election.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Singular only. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'pride' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is the pride of our family.

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Мои повара быстро сломают вашу гордость.
examples.trans: My cooks will quickly break your pride.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
+ accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Television audience member. Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'viewer, spectator' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наш зритель больше любит криминальные новости.
examples.trans: Our audience prefers crime news much more.
The viewers want to see a real chef.

examples.text: Все зрители будут свидетелями нашего спора.
examples.trans: All viewers will be witnesses of our bet.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

обижать.gloss: to hurt, to offend, to bully

meanings.en: to hurt, to mistreat, to offend
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hurt, to offend, to bully', paired with 'обидеть'.

examples.text: Ребята, я понимаю, работа у вас такая. Но детей обижать нехорошо.
examples.trans: Guys, I understand, that's the job you have. But hurting children isn't right.

meanings.en: to pay for, to pay off (+ accusative)
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay, to pay off', paired with 'оплачивать'.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt!

examples.text: Он уже оплатил счёт в ресторане.
examples.trans: He has already paid the bill at the restaurant.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины! Клянусь, весь долг!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt! I swear, the whole debt!

meanings.en: to treat, to handle, to regard (+ к + dative)
meanings.note: относиться бережно к... = to treat with care

examples.text: Он всегда хорошо относится к людям.
Книга новая, мы её только что получили. Пожалуйста, относитесь к ней бережно.
examples.trans: The book is new, we just received it. Please treat it carefully.

отработать.gloss: to work off (a debt), to put in (hours)

meanings.en: to work off (a debt or favour), to pay back by working
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to work off (a debt), to put in (hours)', paired with 'отрабатывать'.

meanings.en: to work (a shift or set time)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to work off (a debt), to put in (hours)', paired with 'отрабатывать'.

examples.text: Я тебе всё отработала на тех выборах.
examples.trans: I paid you back in full at that election.

examples.text: Не надо мне сейчас на совесть давить. Я тебе всё отработала на тех выборах.
examples.trans: Don't try to make me feel guilty now. I paid you back in full at that election.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

поспорить.gloss: to make a bet, wager, argue

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'спорить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to make a bet', forming an aspectual pair with 'спорить'.

examples.text: Я поспорил, что он сбежит сам.
examples.trans: I bet that he will run away on his own.

meanings.note: Asks about the reason. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly
As a reply. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: сбежать из-под ареста = to escape house arrest

examples.text: Да, он сбежал, чтобы спасти моего ребёнка.
examples.trans: Yes, he escaped custody to save my child.
The prisoner escaped from prison at night.

examples.text: Ты думал, что легко сбежишь отсюда?
examples.trans: Did you think that you would easily escape from here?

meanings.note: Someone who saw what happened. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видетель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'witness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Сломать руку = to break one's arm. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: morning or afternoon shift at school or work

examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.

examples.text: А у нас сегодня вторая смена.
examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Perfective of мочь. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be able, to manage', paired with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bet, wager, dispute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a bet, wager, dispute.
I will definitely win this bet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to argue, to dispute', paired with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.
examples.trans: We will definitely cope with this too.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на ужин?
examples.trans: What do we have for dinner today?

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Целый день = all day long. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('whole, entire').
Not broken. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('whole, entire').

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.

examples.text: Илья Олегович! Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: Ilya Olegovich! I can't walk around here all day.

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: В два часа = at two o'clock. Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.
В два часа = at two o'clock. Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week
Core Russian prep meaning 'in (time); through' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
